scenario: AITA for not jumping up and helping my parents bring in the groceries? I'm an adult and I pay rent if that helps. | I'm 33 years old and I've pretty much always lived with my parents. To me there's no shame in it because it's super cheap (they charge me $200, which honestly would be market rate where we live) and it has everything I want and need without the hassle of having to look for a new place to live. We get along most of the time but honestly I just avoid them. Recently the toilet flooded in my bathroom which means they are having to remodel my section of the house so we "run into" each other a lot more than when I used to lock myself in my room most of the time. Well today my parents went to Costco. When they got home I was sitting on the couch playing Apex and my mom asked me to get up and help them bring in groceries. I told her in a minute. I was honestly too into my game to notice that they made several trips back and forth and finally my dad told me to get my ass up. I told him I would in a minute. He said a minute is now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. It turned into a huge shouting match and now they are checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday (which is basically impossible). Of course they brought up my younger brother who is married with two kids and was just promoted at his job. They have their golden child of course but to throw his shit in my face is bullshit. I mean I guess I could have gotten up and helped them but to me because I pay rent that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole in this situation?

That should give me some rights, like having a private space and not being obligated to help with household chores. However, living with others means there are shared responsibilities. Even though I'm paying rent, it's still a family home, and there might be expectations about contributing to the household beyond just paying rent. When my mom asked me to help bring in groceries, I was playing a game and told her I'd do it in a minute. That seems reasonable, but I didn't notice that they were making multiple trips. My dad got frustrated and escalated the situation by grabbing the controller. That led to a shouting match and now they're checking into a hotel, expecting me to find a place by Friday, which is unrealistic. I also feel resentful because they're comparing me to my younger brother, who is doing well. This makes me feel like I'm not good enough, especially since I'm still living with them at 33. On the other hand, I can see that my parents might feel taken for granted. They're remodeling my section of the house because of the plumbing issue, which probably means they're already dealing with some stress. When I didn't help with the groceries, it might have felt like I wasn't contributing to the household, even though I pay rent. I also need to consider the dynamics of our relationship. I've mostly avoided them, which might have led to tension. The fact that I locked myself in my room most of the time suggests that there's already some underlying conflict or discomfort between us. In this situation, both parties seem to have contributed to the conflict. I was engrossed in my game and didn't notice their need for help, which led to frustration on their part. On the other hand, they could have communicated their frustration more calmly instead of grabbing the controller and starting a shouting match. Ultimately, the situation highlights the importance of communication and mutual respect in any living arrangement. Both parties need to express their needs and feelings without resorting to anger or passive-aggressive behavior.
